_doc: Thúy Vi Tông cast, part 1: the Nguyên Anh, the Kết Đan and the dead of the lineage (tiers A and B).

people.gloss: Lam is the blue mist on a mountain
people.role: Head of Thúy Vi Tông; the man who brought the sect down off the ridge
people.appearance: A small, round-shouldered man in a grey robe that is always damp at the hem, with a tea-stained thumb and the White Cloud Whisk pushed through his belt like a fly-swat.
people.backstory: Ngu Lam Sơn was born in 640 above a tea stall in Lam Yên Thị, the market that grew in the haze below the old seat (A040). Phùng Yên Hà (phung_yen_ha) took him into the outer gate at nine because he could sit in the mist all day without growing bored. He never learned a killing art. In the Haze-and-Pine War he carried pills to the Cold Ford, and he carried them again in 901 (C165). The founder died in 1000 at 640, her pulse gone thin and hard as wire in her last years. Cù Thúy Bách (cu_thuy_bach) refused the headship and named him. He took the White Cloud Whisk (C173) and walked in the haze for a hundred days before giving his first order (A045). The order was to go down. He had found that the green breath the sect is named for pools thickest over the empty post town of Cổ Dịch, where the road had been given up to the forest (N-thuy_vi-01). He moved the sect there between 1001 and 1006 (N-thuy_vi-03). He rules by walking: every council of the sect is held on a path. In 1195 he planted the Heir's Garden (N-thuy_vi-08), and he means to step down when it is judged.
people.wants: To hand the sect to someone who will keep it gentle, then walk into the haze and not come back for a long time.
people.secret: He read the founder's pulse in her last year and felt in it what a Wood root feels on Metal ground; he believes the ridge wore her life down. He moved the sect for that reason, and he has let Cù Thúy Bách believe he moved it for the vein. She knows the same thing, and neither has said it to the other.

people.role: Grand elder; keeper of the Cliff Hall on the old seat, the founder's grave and the founder's pine
people.appearance: Tall and bony, with hands cracked like bark and grey hair cut at the jaw; she wears the old ridge robe of undyed hemp, and it is dry, because she will not stand in the haze.
people.backstory: Cù Thúy Bách was born in 610 to a jade-cutter's family that served the sect on its ridge, and she is the oldest person Thúy Vi has. Phùng Yên Hà (phung_yen_ha) took her in 626, the first ridge child to survive three winters in the founder's school. For nearly four hundred years Cù was the founder's hands. She planted the cypress walk on the ridge, held the inner gate through both wars with Tùng Đào (C135, C165), and nursed the founder through her last century. When Phùng died in 1000 (C173), the sect expected Cù to take the whisk. She refused it and named Ngu Lam Sơn (ngu_lam_son), the quiet one, because she wanted to stay on the ridge with the founder's tree. His first order was to leave it. She did not go down. Since 1006 the old seat has been the Cliff Hall (N-thuy_vi-03). She keeps it with a few dozen people: the founder's grave, the founder's pine that grows sideways out of the rock, and the life trees of every disciple who joined before the move. She also keeps a teaching that the sect calls harsh and she calls honest. She is the last of the founder's first disciples. She trains her disciples hard and sends them down to win. She made the boy Hoàn Cô Bách sleep on stone through three winters, and let the fever take two of his year-mates because the rule said to harden them.
people.wants: To see her disciple Hoàn Cô Bách named heir, so the sect remembers what the ridge made it. Failing that, to be buried beside the founder and never moved.
people.secret: She nursed the founder's last century and watched her stiffen like bark, a Wood root starved on Metal ground. She believes the ridge shortened Phùng's life, and she has never said it, because saying it would mean the move was right.

people.role: Master of the Furnace Hall; keeper of the Green Furnace, the maker of Thúy Vi's pills
people.appearance: A lean man with soot in the creases of his knuckles and a green tint to his lips from three centuries of tasting pills.
people.backstory: Úy Thanh Diễm grew up among the charcoal clamps of Thiêu Thán Thôn and could judge a fire by its smoke before he could read. At twenty he walked south to learn from Cao Đan Hà (cao_dan_ha), the greatest alchemist of the age, and kept her furnaces for twenty years. In 920 he came back from an errand to find her dead in her abode beside the pill that killed her (C022). He left without touching it. Thúy Vi took him in at forty, a late start, because Âu Dương Thanh Lô (au_duong_thanh_lo) saw how he fed a fire. He learned the green flame in eleven years. In 932 he watched his second master die at Bách Thảo Viện (V029), trying to hold a cauldron of fire that green flame could not tame. He has kept the Green Furnace lit ever since. When the sect went down the mountain in 1006 he carried the furnace on his back, still burning, and Cù Thúy Bách (cu_thuy_bach) has not forgiven it. He reached Nguyên Anh over that fire in 1150 (N-thuy_vi-10). Thúy Vi's pills are his: clean, slow and trusted. He tastes every batch.
people.wants: To brew the pill that killed Cao Đan Hà correctly, so that her last work is not a poison. For that he needs her Purple Smoke Furnace (Tử Yên Lô) from her lost abode.
people.secret: He knows what the pill was meant to do: carry a Nguyên Anh through the Hóa Thần tribulation. He believes he can make it, and he has told no one, least of all the head.

people.role: First elder of Thúy Vi Tông; master of the Field Hall: grain, herbs and spirit fields
people.appearance: Broad and slow, brown as a field in winter, with lime-burn scars on both forearms and soil under his nails that never washes out.
people.backstory: Quyền Thanh Lam grew up at the lime kilns of Thiêu Hôi Thôn, which has more Earth in its ground than any other village of the sect, and he still smells faintly of burnt stone. Phùng Yên Hà (phung_yen_ha) took him at twelve for the fields, not the hall. He has been first elder since 1040, because nobody else would keep the sect's grain, herbs and spirit fields with the same patience. In 1001 he was the first elder to agree with Ngu Lam Sơn (ngu_lam_son) about going down, and he did the work. He broke the founder's terraces into carts and carried the soil of the ridge gardens down in baskets. In 1006 he rewrote the outer gate's primer for the deep loam of the post town (N-thuy_vi-03). Wherever he travels he carries a field, a nine-square plot that unfolds from his seal. His Dao partner is the herb-keeper Khổng Đương Quy (khong_duong_quy). Their daughter Quyền Tiểu Mạch (quyen_tieu_mach) is the only child either of them wanted. He is old for Kết Đan and has stopped trying for Nguyên Anh, which he says is the same as being content.
people.wants: To see the sect's fields feed it without buying a single grain, and to see his daughter reach Kết Đan before he dies.
people.secret: In 1006 he held back three baskets of the ridge's soil and buried them under the head's new hall, at Cù Thúy Bách's request, so that the founder's ground would lie under the sect wherever it went. Ngu does not know.

people.role: Warden of the Cold Ford Hall at Hàn Tân Thành; the sect's hawk on the Tùng Đào border
people.appearance: A weathered, thick-necked man with a fisher's squint, a white scar through one eyebrow from the ice of 904, and the quay lamp hung at his hip, unlit by day.
people.backstory: Hướng Dạ Đăng was born in Hàn Tân Thành in 870 as a subject of Tùng Đào Cung. His fisher family had kept the name of the warden who fell on the quay in 672, Hướng Đông Lâm (huong_dong_lam), for eight generations. His grandmother paid the resin tax in fish because she had no resin (A041). At eleven he swam the river mouth to the hills to join Thúy Vi. He was a Trúc Cơ in the Cold Ford War (C165), under Tân Hàn Chu (tan_han_chu), who died the winter before the ford came home (N-thuy_vi-06). In 905 he dug his ancestor's lamp out from under the quay stones where the fishers had hidden it (C166), and the fishers lit lamps on every boat for a month (A044). He has held the Cold Ford Hall since 960. He thinks the Pivot's writs are a game Tùng Đào plays better. In his view the ford came back with a writ only because Đỗ Tinh Hà (do_tinh_ha) was ashamed of the first one, and the next war will not wait for paper. Every winter he drills the coast's disciples on the ice of the river mouth. His wife drowned in 1180. His daughter Hướng Vãn Chu (huong_van_chu) holds a plot in the Heir's Garden, and he wants her to win it.
people.wants: To push the border back to Lô Khẩu marsh and the old resin-tax villages, and to see his daughter head of the sect.
people.secret: In 1172 he caught a Tùng Đào patrol on the ice of the river mouth and put all six of them under it. The Pivot never heard, and Tùng Đào believes they deserted.

people.gloss: Diêm for the salt; hải tảo is sargassum, a seaweed in the herb book
people.role: Keeper of the port house at Yên Ba Thành: the sect's sea trade and the cape's coast
people.appearance: Short, brown and salt-cracked, with a sailor's rolling walk, a whale-cast brass lock on a cord at her throat and a laugh that carries across a harbour.
people.backstory: When the Pivot's fleets broke Thôn Hải in 781, the pirates who had wintered in the cove below Ẩn Loan Thôn vanished in one night. They left a chest of salt and a three-year-old girl (A026). The villagers fed her and said nothing, as they had fed the pirates (A025). Ngu Lam Sơn (ngu_lam_son), then a Kết Đan carrying pills down the cape, found her eating kelp on the beach and took her up to the ridge (N-thuy_vi-04). The sect names its foundlings from the herb book. It named her Hải Tảo for the seaweed and Diêm, by a pun, for the salt. She grew up the sect's sailor. She keeps the port house at Yên Ba Thành, which ships Thúy Vi's pills down the coast and up the strait. She has more friends among the boatwrights and smugglers of the cape than any elder has in the halls. She is 422 and has perhaps eighty years left. In those years she means to learn whose daughter she is. She is fairly sure she knows already: the pirate lord Ô Kình Hải (o_kinh_hai), who died in the Purge the year she was left. The port house takes a tenth of every smuggler's cargo that lands under its lamp, and she calls it a lamp fee.
people.wants: To find her father's sabre Kình Nha at the ruin of Thôn Hải Môn far in the south (place 217), and to learn whether the chest was left for her or only with her.
people.secret: The chest of salt had a false bottom. Inside was a sea chart of the southern islands in Ô Kình Hải's hand. She has kept it for four hundred years and never sailed it.

people.gloss: Green moss (Vương Duy: the returning light shines again on the green moss)
people.role: The head's true disciple and the sect's best healer-grower; holds the first plot of the Heir's Garden
people.appearance: Slight and soft-spoken, with grey-green eyes and her sleeves always rolled; a mirror furred with moss hangs at her waist.
people.backstory: Thiệu Thanh Đài was born in Phục Linh Thôn among the poria diggers, who find the fungus by its smell under old pines, and she has their patience. She came to the outer gate in 1052, one of the first generation raised wholly at the new seat. She has never lived on the ridge and does not miss it. Ngu Lam Sơn (ngu_lam_son) chose her as his disciple in 1060. He says it was because she kept a moss garden alive through a drought by talking to it; she says she only watered it at night. She is the sect's best healer after Dư Tục Đoạn (du_tuc_doan), and its best grower after no one. She reached Kết Đan in 1180, and her master gave her the moss mirror with the line the sect lives by: the returning light shines again on the green moss. In 1195 he gave her one of the three plots of the Heir's Garden (N-thuy_vi-08). She has planted moss. Hoàn Cô Bách (hoan_co_bach) says moss is what grows where nothing else will. Her first disciple is the foundling Kiển Viễn Chí (kien_vien_chi), who wants the headship more than she does.
people.wants: To keep the sect as her master made it, quiet and green, whether or not she is the one who leads it.
people.secret: She does not want to be head. She planted moss so that she would lose, and she is afraid her disciple has guessed.

people.role: The grand elder's true disciple and the Cliff Hall's champion; holds the second plot of the Heir's Garden
people.appearance: Tall and hard-faced, burnt dark by the ridge wind, with a cypress banner-pole across his back and hands calloused from cutting stone.
people.backstory: Hoàn Cô Bách was born on the ridge in 1020, fourteen years after the sect left it, to a jade-cutter who stayed. He is the only true disciple of Thúy Vi who has never lived at the new seat. Cù Thúy Bách (cu_thuy_bach) took him at six and raised him on the Cliff Hall's teaching: roots that split rock, a body hardened by the Metal wind, sleep on stone. At forty he walked down to the new seat for the inner gate's contest, beat every disciple there with a cypress pole, and walked back up the same night. He has the ridge in his root, Metal beside his Wood, and he does not hide it. He thinks the new seat breeds soft people in a warm garden, and that the sect would have lost the Cold Ford War if it had fought it from Cổ Dịch. In 1195 the head gave him a plot of the Heir's Garden (N-thuy_vi-08). He did not plant it at the seat. He carried a cypress seedling up to a crack in the rock above the founder's pine and planted it there, where nothing grows. It is alive.
people.wants: To be named heir and bring the sect's heart back up the mountain, or at least the inner gate's teaching.
people.secret: He is afraid of the haze. As a boy he was lost in it on the slope for a night and nearly drowned in a ditch, and the ridge is the only place he can breathe. He has never told Cù.

people.role: Master of the Array Hall; the elder who taught the Haze Walk away
people.appearance: A wiry old man who walks fast and talks faster, with array chalk on his cuffs.
people.backstory: Born in the river mists of Phù Kiều Trấn, Tất Hành Vụ took to formations because the haze already looked to him like an array. He laid the new seat's Lotus Throne and Spring Return arrays in 1006, and he alone can read the Haze Walk's ninth layer. In 1048 he taught the walk to his sworn brother, a road guard, who took it to the cape and founded Vụ Ẩn Môn on it (N-thuy_vi-07). Half the elders call it theft. He calls it the only good the walk has ever done. His granddaughter Tất Quế Lạc (tat_que_lac) is his disciple.
people.wants: To hear the Haze Walk's ninth layer read correctly by someone other than himself before he dies.
people.secret: He is teaching the ninth layer in pieces to his granddaughter Tất Quế Lạc, folded into her chalk drills, and has told the Array Hall it is only a game.

people.appearance: Small and stooped, always smelling of angelica root, with a burn scar along one cheek from 932.
people.backstory: Khổng Đương Quy was twelve and a servant orphan of Bách Thảo Viện when its fire cauldron burst in 932 (V029). Âu Dương Thanh Lô (au_duong_thanh_lo) threw her out of the hall with the academy's seed gourd in her arms before the roof came down on him. Thúy Vi carried the academy's herb books to the seat, and her with them. She has kept the books and the sect's herb gardens ever since. She still means to rebuild Bách Thảo Viện one day, as her herb name says. She married Quyền Thanh Lam (quyen_thanh_lam) in 1100.
people.wants: A shed of Bách Thảo Viện rebuilt, with its books under one roof.
people.secret: She replants the academy's lost herbs in rows across Quyền Thanh Lam's fields, among what he takes for weeds, and he has begun to plough around them without a word.

people.role: Master of the Hall of Rules; ridge-trained, called the Avalanche
people.appearance: Square, unsmiling and grey at the temples; he stands very straight and speaks in the fewest words he can.
people.backstory: Nhạc Chính Hành was nineteen and a Luyện Khí outer disciple, home for the New Year, when the avalanche buried the upper street of Vân Gian Trấn and his family in it (V031). He dug for nine days. Afterwards Cù Thúy Bách (cu_thuy_bach) took him up to the ridge, and the Cliff Hall made him hard and exact. He has kept the Hall of Rules at the new seat since 1150 and judges as the ridge would: by the rule, not the person. Since 1190 he has bought Vụ Ẩn Môn's head's pages on what passes under the mist, paid in patrols on the Đồng Sơn road and in his silence whenever the tithe is raised.
people.wants: A sect where no exception is left to renew.
people.secret: Every decade he signs the Hall's exception for Quản Ảnh Hồ without reading it, the one rule he bends, because he cannot bring himself to ask what her mirror method does.

people.role: Keeper of the Marten Yard on Ngân Điêu Đài, where silver martens are bred to find spirit herbs
people.appearance: Sharp-faced and quick, with a fur collar that turns out to be a live silver marten asleep.
people.backstory: Lô Dã Hương grew up hunting matsutake under the pines of Tùng Nhung Thôn with a tame marten on her shoulder. Ngu Lam Sơn (ngu_lam_son) took her as his disciple in 1010 for her nose. She runs the sect's Marten Yard on Ngân Điêu Đài, where silver martens are bred to sniff out spirit herbs. She trusts animals over people and says so. Her martens find a hundred-year ginseng in a season, and she sells their pups to Hồng Lô Cốc for more than the ginseng is worth. Every pup she sells to the vassal will never breed.
people.wants: A pup in her line that finds a ginseng a thousand years old.
people.secret: She sells Hồng Lô Cốc pups she has quietly spayed, so that no vassal ever breeds its own silver marten line.

people.role: The sect's envoy to the Pivot, the vassals and Tùng Đào
people.appearance: Elegant and quick-eyed, in a robe cut in the Tùng Đào fashion and dyed Thúy Vi green.
people.backstory: Biện Vãn Tình was born in Tùng Hạ Thị, Tùng Đào's market under the pines, to a Thúy Vi pill trader and a local scribe, and she speaks both sects' courtesies without an accent. Úy Thanh Diễm (uy_thanh_diem) trained her in the Furnace Hall until it was clear she sold a pill better than she brewed one. Since 1140 she has carried the sect's letters to the Pivot, the vassals and across the border. She has kept the Cold Ford quiet through four of Hướng Dạ Đăng's (huong_da_dang) winters. She thinks the warden will start a war and that the head will let him finish it. She tells Tùng Đào when the warden drills, and calls it courtesy.
people.wants: A peace so long that her letters are the only thing crossing the border.
people.secret: She tells Hồ Tùng Nguyệt the dates of the warden's winter drills so that Tùng Đào's patrols stay off the ice, and calls it keeping the peace.

people.role: Guest elder for refining: jade-cutter, needle-smith and furnace-mender at Bích Ngọc Khoáng
people.appearance: Grey with stone dust and thick in the wrist, missing the last finger of his left hand to a jade saw.
people.backstory: Lã Trác Thạch was born at the green jade mine below the old seat (A037), where the rock is half Metal, and his root came out Metal and Earth with no Wood in it at all. Thúy Vi could not take him into its lineage, so it hired him. He has been the sect's guest elder for refining since 1030. He cuts the jade for its seals, forges its pill needles and mends the iron bands of its green furnaces. He lives at the mine, not the seat, and goes up to the Cliff Hall to drink with Hoàn Cô Bách (hoan_co_bach), whose father worked his seam.
people.wants: A jade seam without a flaw, and one seal cut from it that he would never sell.
people.secret: He is slipping jade pill needles, which bend, in among the steel ones to see whether the Furnace Hall notices; Úy Thanh Diễm tastes every batch and has so far said nothing.

people.role: Elder of the Healing House at Lam Yên Thị; the sect's bone-setter and the Green Door Day's healer
people.appearance: A long-armed, gentle man with a healer's satchel and green-stained fingertips.
people.backstory: Dư Tục Đoạn was raised at Thanh Nang Đường, the healers' hall in the forest, and was twenty-one when its last head died in seclusion without naming an heir (V018). The other healers took their satchels to Hồng Lô Cốc. He walked the other way, to Thúy Vi, because he had heard its pills were cleaner, and Úy Thanh Diễm (uy_thanh_diem) took him into the Furnace Hall. He is the sect's bone-setter. Once a month, on the Green Door Day, he sits at the sect's door in Lam Yên Thị and treats anyone for nothing. That is how the sect found the foundling Kiển Viễn Chí (kien_vien_chi).
people.wants: A Green Door Day every day of the month.
people.secret: He fills the poor's satchels on the Green Door Day with the Furnace Hall's wound pills from his own stock, and Tề Tử Tô has begun to count the shortfall in her batches.

people.gloss: Mist and rosy cloud; yên hà is also the love of landscape
people.cause: lifespan worn down on the Metal ground of the ridge, which starved her Wood; died at 640
people.role: Founder of Thúy Vi Tông (year 500, at 140); lies on the ridge under her pine
people.backstory: Phùng Yên Hà was a painter's daughter who never painted. She walked into landscapes instead, which is what yên hà means: an incurable love of mist and mountains. In 500, at 140, she came to the empty mountain of Không Sơn Viện. Its last master, Thôi Bất Kiến (thoi_bat_kien), had no heir and gave her the hills of Thanh Loan Lĩnh, his whisk and his only student, Tống Tọa Vân (tong_toa_van) (C100). She founded Thúy Vi Tông the same year (C010). She built her halls on the high ridge where she could see every hill she had been given, and she planted a pine in the rock by the gate. When the old master died in the empty academy in 520, she left it as it was, unlocked and unlooted (A038). She took the cape (C115), founded Yên Ba Thành (C120) and Mục Ca Thành (C139), lost the Cold Ford to Tùng Đào in 672 (C136) and took it back with the Pivot's writ in 905 (C166). Her Dao partner was the alchemist Âu Dương Thanh Lô (au_duong_thanh_lo). She died at 640 (C173), stiff and grey in her last century, and was buried under her pine.

people.role: The first Furnace Master and the founder's Dao partner; wrote the Green Furnace Canon
people.backstory: In the 520s the sect was too poor to buy volcano fire from the isles, so its first Furnace Master taught himself to burn spirit wood green and wrote the Green Furnace Canon. He fired the Green Furnace in 540. In 932 Bách Thảo Viện sent for him to hold a cauldron of untamed fire. Green flame could not hold it, and he threw the child Khổng Đương Quy (khong_duong_quy) out of the hall before the roof fell (V029). His last disciple, Úy Thanh Diễm (uy_thanh_diem), keeps his furnace lit.

people.role: The first Warden of the Cold Ford
people.backstory: A fisher's son of Hàn Tân Thành whom the founder raised to Kết Đan and made the first Warden of the Cold Ford. When Tùng Đào came without a writ in 668 (C135), he held the quays for four years. When the Pivot let the conquest stand in 672 (C136), he would not leave them, and he died beside his lamp, which the fishers hid under the quay stones. His family stayed under Tùng Đào's resin tax for 233 years and kept his name (N-thuy_vi-05). Hướng Dạ Đăng (huong_da_dang) is of his line.

people.backstory: Tân Hàn Chu led the boats in the Cold Ford War (C165). In the winter of 904 she took forty disciples across the ice of the river mouth at night, under Tùng Đào's arrays, and the ice broke. The ford came home the next year (C166) without her. Her disciple Hướng Dạ Đăng (huong_da_dang) found her body at the thaw (N-thuy_vi-06). The coast still calls the river mouth's ice the Boat in the Cold.

people.role: Keeper of Lam Triều Các, the sect's coast pavilion
people.backstory: Mẫn Triều Âm kept Lam Triều Các, the sect's coast pavilion, where the cape's boatwrights learned to read the tide. Thôn Hải's pirates landed at night in 744, burned the pavilion and carried off its disciples (V010). She held the point until their boats had gone and was found on it in the morning. The boatwrights still light a fire on the point on that night. Cù Thúy Bách (cu_thuy_bach) was her sworn sister.
